exact_theorem.graph: G is a finite simple graph with at least one cycle and with every edge having an endpoint of degree at most3. Fix q>=2 and s in(0,1), s!=1/q. If s<1/q also assume G bipartite. In particular every actual bipartite K4 subdivision satisfies these conditions.
exact_theorem.base_pair: kappa0 uniform on{1,...,q}; lambda_s(x,x)=s/q, lambda_s(x,y)=(1-s)/(q(q-1)) for x!=y. Every entry is positive. Let m=|E(G)| and I_q(s)=s log(qs)+(1-s)log(q(1-s)/(q-1)).
exact_theorem.strict_gap: The fitted finite Potts law mu_s has every actual edge lambda_s and singleton kappa0, and Delta_s=m I_q(s)-D(mu_s||kappa0^V)>0. It is also the unique maximum-entropy law for these prescribed tables, by the Gibbs KL identity.
exact_theorem.full_table_neighborhood: There is an open neighborhood U of(lambda_s,kappa0), relative to compatible symmetric strictly positive finite pair tables lambda with common singleton kappa, such that every(lambda,kappa) in U has a full-support law tau on the actual q^{V(G)} with every singleton kappa, every actual edge exactly lambda, and D(tau||kappa^V)<m D(lambda||kappa^2). Thus the result includes non-Potts pair tables and nonuniform singleton laws near every positive nonindependent Potts target, not only near independence.
exact_theorem.triple_extension_nonvacuity: For q>=3, the neighborhood can be chosen so that every symmetric pair table in it itself has a strictly positive exchangeable triple extension. Therefore this open family is genuinely inside the requested triple-extendible input class. The entropy witness theorem does not require that triple extension as a proof ingredient.

proof.argument: The preceding candidate gives exact fit using finite interactions J_e lying between0 and theta(s)=log((q-1)s/(1-s)). At a hypothetical zero edge v-w choose its degree<=3 endpoint v. With two active neighbors a,b, exact agreements on va and vb force J_va=J_vb. For the positive sign, their color is a conditional maximizer; for the negative sign it is a minimizer. The comparison with the color of w is strict on the actual event X_a=X_b!=X_w, which has positive probability because all configurations have positive probability and a,b,w are distinct actual vertices. With one active neighbor strictness holds on X_a!=X_w. With no active neighbors agreement is1/q. In all cases strictness contradicts the appropriate zero-face KKT inequality for s!=1/q. Hence every J_e is nonzero. This includes q=2; the unequal-neighbor configuration alone need not be strict, but the equal-neighbor/different-w event is.

proof.step: 2. Every cycle edge is strictly inside its interaction cap
proof.argument: Delete the interaction on any edge e=uv lying on a cycle. The remaining graph has an alternate u-v path, whose interactions are all nonzero by Step1. The weighted two-color conditioning from the base proof gives the weak correct correlation sign in every conditioning. The event that every vertex receives color1 or2 has positive probability. Conditional on this event, the entire removed-edge graph is a zero-field Ising model. Its high-temperature correlation numerator contains a strictly positive term from the alternate path, while the denominator is positive. In the ferromagnetic case this gives a strictly positive correlation; in the bipartite antiferromagnetic case the bipartition flip gives a strictly negative correlation between u and v. Averaging all conditionings preserves this strict sign, so the removed-edge Potts agreement a0 is strictly above1/q for positive interactions and strictly below1/q for negative interactions. Restoring the cap J_e=theta(s) would yield agreement strictly above s in the former case and strictly below s in the latter, contradicting cap KKT. Thus0<J_e<theta(s) in the positive regime, and theta(s)<J_e<0 in the negative regime, for every cycle edge. Bridge edges need not be strictly below their cap.

proof.step: 3. Interaction covariance is positive definite and exact fits glue analytically
proof.argument: Let h_e(x)=1[x_u=x_v]. Under any full-support law the covariance of these m edge statistics is positive definite. Indeed, if a linear combination sum_e c_e h_e were constant on all configurations, restrict configurations to colors1 and2 and write h_e=(1+sigma_u sigma_v)/2. The distinct simple-edge Walsh monomials sigma_u sigma_v are linearly independent modulo constants on{+1,-1}^V, forcing every c_e=0. A nonconstant statistic has positive variance under full support. Consequently the Hessian of logZ is positive definite at every finite interaction vector, and its gradient is globally injective by strict convexity. At the exact fit, the equations E_J h_e=s for every edge have an invertible Jacobian. The real analytic implicit function theorem therefore gives a locally analytic exact-fit vector J(s). Global injectivity ensures that local inverses agree wherever they overlap and agree with the box minimizers already supplied by the base proof. At s=1/q the root J=0 is also locally analytic and unique. Thus the fitted family is continuous and locally analytic on the applicable interval:0<s<1 for bipartite G, and1/q<=s<1 for a general G, with a local analytic inverse at1/q. No antiferromagnetic fitted family is asserted on a nonbipartite graph. This regularity is proved here and is not silently assumed in the base entropy interpolation.

With Z normalized relative to kappa0^V, write C(s)=D(mu_s||kappa0^V)=s sum_e J_e(s)-log Z(J(s)). Exact agreements give dC/ds=sum_e J_e(s): the terms containing derivatives of J cancel. At s0=1/q the product law has C(s0)=0; the cap bounds imply J(s)->0 as s->s0, consistent with the analytic inverse there. Since I_q'(s)=theta(s), Delta_s=integral_{s0}^{s}[m theta(u)-sum_e J_e(u)]du. In the positive regime every interaction is<=theta(u) and at least one cycle interaction is strictly smaller, so the integrand is strictly positive. In the negative regime every interaction is>=theta(u) and a cycle interaction is strictly larger, so the integrand is strictly negative but the integration direction is reversed. Both give Delta_s>0 at every interior nonindependent target. The coefficient remains sharp in the wider graph class because forests attain equality; strictness is the extra cyclic slack.

proof.step: 5. Full singleton/table gauge, independent of the varying reference
proof.argument: Fix once and for all an orthonormal basis f_1,...,f_{q-1} of mean-zero functions under the uniform kappa0. Choose an orientation of every actual edge. Use every unary statistic f_i(X_v) and every oriented-edge product f_i(X_u)f_j(X_v). Their covariance under the product law kappa0^V is the identity: distinct edges or unary/edge combinations have an unmatched centered vertex factor; on an individual edge product-basis orthogonality applies. Thus these statistics are affinely independent modulo constants on the complete configuration space. Their covariance is consequently positive definite under the full-support base law mu_s as well. Exponentially tilt mu_s by all these statistics. The expectation map has this invertible covariance Jacobian at zero tilt. It therefore realizes every sufficiently nearby target moment vector by the implicit function theorem. The basis remains fixed while kappa changes. The required target unary moments are sum_x kappa(x)f_i(x), and required edge-product moments are sum_xy lambda(x,y)f_i(x)f_j(y). Unary moments and all edge-product moments together reconstruct every full actual edge table, because{1,f_1,...,f_{q-1}} is a basis. Compatibility of lambda and kappa is explicitly retained. No averaged-edge constraints or omitted administrative means are substituted.

proof.step: 6. The strict budget survives full-table perturbation
proof.argument: The exact tilted law tau(kappa,lambda) is continuous, in fact analytic in its finite moment coordinates, and tends to mu_s at the base input. For nearby strictly positive kappa and lambda, both D(tau||kappa^V) and mD(lambda||kappa^2) are continuous finite expressions. Their difference at the base is the strictly negative number-Delta_s. Shrinking the compatible input neighborhood therefore retains a gap of at least Delta_s/2. This supplies a genuine open family of exact arbitrary-table witnesses, including nonuniform kappa and non-Potts lambda. It does not specify a graph-independent radius, claim all compatible tables lie in this family, or assert that local neighborhoods cover the full target domain. No numerical surrogate is used for either invertibility or the entropy gap.

proof.step: 7. Positive exchangeable extension around interior Potts inputs for q>=3
proof.argument: For q>=3 let eta_dist be the uniform exchangeable law on ordered triples of three distinct colors, whose pair is the Potts table at s=0. Let eta_eq be the uniform all-equal triple, whose pair has s=1. The IID uniform triple eta_iid has s=1/q and is strictly positive. If0<s<1/q use eta_s=(q s)eta_iid+(1-q s)eta_dist. If1/q<s<1 use eta_s=[(1-s)/(1-1/q)]eta_iid+[1-(1-s)/(1-1/q)]eta_eq. At s=1/q use eta_iid. Every interior eta_s is strictly positive and has pair lambda_s. To extend a nearby symmetric table lambda'=lambda_s+delta, put d_x=sum_y delta(x,y) and keep kappa0 fixed in the following linear expression: Deltaeta(x,y,z)=delta(x,y)kappa0(z)+delta(x,z)kappa0(y)+delta(y,z)kappa0(x)-d_x kappa0(y)kappa0(z)-d_y kappa0(x)kappa0(z)-d_z kappa0(x)kappa0(y). Symmetry is explicit; total mass is zero because sum delta=sum d=0. Summing over z gives exactly delta(x,y), since the extra row-sum terms cancel. Hence eta_s+Deltaeta is exchangeable with pair lambda' and singleton kappa'=kappa0+d. For sufficiently small delta it remains strictly positive on every finite triple. This makes the open family nonvacuous within the requested triple-extendible cone. It does not extend this conclusion to the cone boundary or all tables.

maximum_entropy_identity: For any law rho with the prescribed base edge table lambda_s, E_rho sum_e J_e h_e=s sum_e J_e. Direct Gibbs likelihood expansion yields D(rho||kappa0^V)=D(mu_s||kappa0^V)+D(rho||mu_s). Thus mu_s is the unique entropy-maximizing/full-table KL-minimizing witness; the strict budget is not obtained merely by changing the reference or relaxing the edge marginals.

edge_cases_and_limits.forest: No strict-gap assertion is made for forests, which have exact equality under independent stationary tree constructions. Their universal exact-table property does not need the present openness argument.
edge_cases_and_limits.independence: At s=1/q the Potts gap is zero. This argument does not infer an open neighborhood merely from gap continuity there; the independently completed local-IID theorem is a distinct argument and is not repeated here.
edge_cases_and_limits.zero_pair_masses: The open-neighborhood argument requires0<s<1, positive base entries and finite interactions. It does not assert robust neighborhoods at s=0 or1, where compactness gives the base Potts witness but Hessian/gap limits may differ.
edge_cases_and_limits.disconnected_or_isolated: At least one cyclic component suffices for strictness. Isolated vertices have independent uniform base variables and contribute their unary statistics to the full gauge. Disconnected graph products do not invalidate covariance independence or the exact budget.
edge_cases_and_limits.q2_triple_range: The entropy theorem is valid for all binary s in[0,1] on the stated bipartite graphs, but binary exchangeable triple extension has additional restrictions. Step7 deliberately assumes q>=3 rather than importing an incorrect q2 all-s extension.
